text:
Angel filled with joy, do you know anguish,
guilt, shame, weariness, sobs,
and the vague terrors of those dreadful nights
that crush the heart like crumpled paper?
Angel filled with joy, do you know anguish?

Angel filled with goodness, do you know hatred,
tears of gall and clenched fists,
when vengeance raises its infernal voice
and sets itself up as captain of our faculties?
Angel filled with goodness, do you know hatred?

Angel filled with health, do you know Fever,
which, along the wall of the milky hospital,
walks with weary steps like the exiles,
seeking the scant sun and moving its lips?
Angel filled with health, do you know Fever?

Angel filled with beauty, do you know wrinkles,
and fear of growing old, and that hateful torment
of reading the secret horror of sacrifice
in eyes from which our own once drank?
Angel filled with beauty, do you know wrinkles?

Angel filled with happiness, light, and joy!
Dying David would have asked for healing
from the emanations of your bewitching body;
but from you, angel, I implore only prayers,
angel filled with happiness, light, and joy!

translation.title: Reversibility
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish version of Baudelaire. A stray source glyph following ‘David’ is treated as typographic noise.
